name: Desvenlafaxine
sections: White to off-white powder (succinate monohydrate), soluble in water.

A synthetic form of O-desmethylvenlafaxine, the major active metabolite of venlafaxine; marketed as the succinate salt in extended-release tablets. First approval/introduction: US FDA February 2008 (Wyeth) for major depressive disorder.

Active metabolite of venlafaxine; selectively inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine, potentiating their neurotransmission in the CNS. Receptor / target profile: SNRI approximately 10-fold more potent at serotonin than norepinephrine uptake (SERT Ki 40.2 nM; NET Ki 558.4 nM).
Conjugation (UGT) and minor CYP3A4 oxidation; CYP2D6 not involved

Summary: Bioavailability ~80%; Tmax ~7.5 h (extended release). Low protein binding (~30%). Metabolised mainly by conjugation (minor CYP3A4); little CYP2D6 involvement. Half-life ~11 h. Renally excreted.
